$description: Local AI panel design tokens. Every value here is read by design/panel.mjs and design/build.mjs; nothing is drawn from a literal. Panel.qml is the runtime; this file is the same numbers written down so they can be reviewed, diffed and imported (W3C Design Tokens format, so Tokens Studio for Figma and Penpot's token sets read it as-is).

space.$description: Style.space(n) in Omarchy's Quattro shell. At the shell's default scale space(n) = n px, so 20 = 20 px. The panel uses one grid: every line of text starts and ends on the gutter (20), surfaces sit at the edge (8), so the text inside them lands on the same gutter (20 - 8 = 12).

font.$description: Style.font in the Quattro shell. The panel takes the bar's own family (root.mono), which is a Nerd Font monospace, so every advance is 0.6 em and a label's width is chars x 0.6 x size. Three sizes only: caption for facts and labels, body for a model's name, subtitle for a card's name.

advance.$description: JetBrains Mono's advance width, 600/1000 em. design/panel.mjs uses it to measure a label the way Qt measures a Text's implicitWidth.

captionSmall.$description: caption - 2, a masked secret and a version number

captionLarge.$description: caption - 1, the months under the activity grid and a card's chips

body.$description: a model's name in the hero

subtitle.$description: a running model's name on its card

head.$description: Style.space(16): the height of the top line and of a section name

lineHeight.$description: one line of a Label, Qt's implicitHeight for a Text at a size. 1.4 x size, rounded up.

layout.$description: Panel.qml's own constants, in Style.space() units. The panel is a column 340 px wide, 16 px of air above and below, clipped and flickable.

edge.$description: Style.space(8): the inset of a surface from the panel's edge

gutter.$description: Style.space(20): the one line every label starts and ends on

pad.$description: gutter - edge: a surface's own inset, so its text lands on the gutter

rowH.$description: one plain row: a GPU, a field, an option, a choice

headH.$description: the top line, and a section name

groupGap.$description: Style.space(20): before a section, a button row or an error

blockGap.$description: Style.space(8): before a running model's card or the figures

topGap.$description: Style.space(12): above the first row of a page

chartH.$description: the token line in a hero

slotCrashedH.$description: a crashed card's row, framed in dashes

logo.$description: A mark is a rounded tile with one glyph or one monogram in it: the make of a card on its plate, the family of a model on its card. A monogram rather than a brand image, because the panel draws with a Nerd Font and a tile is the one mark that survives every theme and every width.

tile.$description: the mark on a card's plate

small.$description: the mark on a model's card

mini.$description: the mark on a plain row

gap.$description: between a mark and the text it belongs to

plate.$description: the card a models page is about, as a plate at the top of the page: its mark, its name, what it is, and its memory

model.$description: a model as a card rather than a line: a mark, a name, and its figures under it. Two lines of text need more than a row's 26 px, and the room is the point — a list of models is the one place the panel is read rather than tapped.

gap.$description: between one model card and the next

cell.$description: one day in the activity grid

hairline.$description: the 1 px gaps in the figures grid, and a surface's border

was.$description: The panel as it is today: 22 px rows on a 20 px gutter. Kept here so a before-and-after is drawn by the same renderer from two token sets, and the only difference between the two drawings is these numbers.

nav.$description: What the panel lacks today: a page that remembers where it came from, and a path. A back stack is a page's own history, so going back lands where you were rather than always on home; the path shares the panel's own 16 px head row, so it costs no height.

depth.$description: the pages the head can lead back through: home → hardware → one card → one model

crumb.$description: one segment of the path: caption, on the head row, tappable

segmentGap.$description: between one segment and the next, around its chevron

wall.$description: The full-screen layout: three columns, no row stretched. The panel is 340 px because the bar is a bar, and every row in it was designed for 340; so the full-screen layout shows the panel at 340, the page for the selected row at 704 where the wide rows live, and the rail at 220. 220 + 8 + 340 + 8 + 704 = 1280.

height.$description: the shortest the layout is drawn, so the rail and both columns run the whole window

rail.$description: the index and what is running

pane.$description: the page you are on, exactly as the panel draws it

detail.$description: the page for the selected row: where the wide rows are allowed, and only there

activity.$description: the lifetime grid: a column a week, a row a weekday, a day shaded in four steps by its tokens against the busiest day

levels.$description: alpha over the panel background, one per token step: 1..4. A day with no tokens is blank.

chart.$description: the token line: a dim 1.2 px stroke over a 6% fill, cumulative, rising to the right, the top of the busiest hour at 80% of the height

plot.$description: how much of the height the top of the data reaches

motion.$description: the panel's only motion, all of it small and slow. The glow and the ripple are the only two loops.

period.$description: 3.6 s: the card border breathes between glowFrom and glowTo

step.$description: ten steps a second, too small to see apart, so the panel redraws ten times a second for it rather than sixty

ripple.$description: the bar's nine dots while a model starts: a diagonal wave, one step every 160 ms

wave.$description: the no-model line drifting left, one period every 2.4 s, twenty steps a second, half a pixel a step

copied.$description: how long "copied" stays on a secret value

poll.$description: how often the panel asks the backend for a snapshot

contrast.$description: APCA-W3 0.1.9 lightness contrast (Lc) targets, solved per theme in Model.js tones(). Every text and line colour in the panel is picked by the Lc it must reach on the card surface, so any theme stays readable. Ink is for what matters now, value for what a label names, label for every label, rule for lines and borders that are not text, alert for problems.

color.$description: The panel takes its colours from the active theme; these are the three the studio plots. Every role below is computed by Model.js tones() from the theme, never written by hand, so a theme change is a token change.

surface.$description: Util.alpha(theme, 0.06) over bg: the figures, the chip row, the chart plate

card.$description: Util.alpha(theme, 0.08) over bg: a running model's card, a little above the page

hairline.$description: the 1 px gaps in the figures grid

icon.$description: Nerd Font glyphs, one code point each, from Panel.qml's glyphs map. A glyph is drawn in a 12 px box and never advances a line.
